name: Ariel Sharon
summary: Sharon, Israeli prime minister 2001-2006, announced and carried through the unilateral disengagement from Gaza and four northern West Bank settlements, which the Knesset approved in 2004 and 2005 over opposition from almost half of his own Likud. The record found settles none of the statements in the bank.

territorial-expansion.rationale: His acts split: as housing minister he drove settlement building in the West Bank and Gaza, as prime minister he withdrew from all of Gaza and four northern West Bank settlements.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Told the UN General Assembly in 2005: 'there will be no compromise on the right of the State of Israel to exist as a Jewish state', and that the Land of Israel is the 'identity and right of the Jewish people'.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: His government set a 4 percent deficit target for 2004, to be lowered in following years, and capped real spending growth at 1 percent, through the 2003 recovery plan that cut spending in a recession.

national-self-determination.rationale: Told the UN in 2005 that Palestinians 'are also entitled to freedom and to a national, sovereign existence in a state of their own', and the Jewish people's right to national revival in their homeland; the general principle for every people is not stated.

work-for-welfare.rationale: His government's 2003 Economy Arrangements Law cut income support and tightened the employment test to push benefit recipients into the labor market.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Said Israel 'will not remain in all the places where it is today' in a future agreement and that 'we have to make concessions for the sake of peace', while claiming an 'eternal and unimpeachable' Jewish right to the Land of Israel.

majority-settlement.rationale: As housing minister (1990-92) 73 percent of housing starts were government-sponsored and targeted to the regions he favored for Jewish settlement in the West Bank and Gaza, which were Palestinian-majority; later, as prime minister, he promised no new settlements.

notes: Second pass after the integrator's review. The disengagement votes alone settle nothing without inference; the 2005 UN speech, the Herzliya speech, housing starts as minister, the Lebanon invasion and the 2003 economic law settle the eight statements answered. The Likud member vote of May 2004 (about 60 percent against, per Al Jazeera) and the 72-26 rejection of a national referendum show tactics, not a position on direct votes. Barrier decisions (2002-03) and Kadima's founding (2005) settle no statement in the bank. Statements not listed stay null. Themes searched: settlements, Gaza and West Bank withdrawal, Lebanon, the barrier, UN speeches, the 2003 economic programme, interviews 2000-2005 (terrorism, Jerusalem); religion and state, civil liberties and trade found nothing of his own.
